analyst_view.overall: Early view: This is a Friday night game between two in-form sides: Palladino's Bologna had won four in a row before the break, including 4-2 at Milan in October, and Gasperini's Roma were unbeaten after 11 games. Roma host Sporting in the Champions League four days later. Orsolini is back for Bologna; Roma should have Svilar and Dybala back by then, but Pellegrini's return will take longer.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. I lean slightly higher: Roma have scored 2.8 a game away, and their away games average 3.8 goals. Bologna score freely in this form, and Gasperini's Roma do not sit back to protect a lead.

corners.text: The site expects 9.2 corners. Bologna's home games have averaged about 10.6 and Roma's away games about 8.8, so the number is fair. Roma win far more corners at home than away, which keeps me from going higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. I lean higher: Bologna's home games have averaged almost six cards, among the most in the league, and this is a game between two teams in the top eight. Bologna's games overall have averaged about 4.2 cards, among the highest in Serie A.

shots.text: The site expects 25.2 shots. I lean slightly higher because Roma's away games have averaged about 28 shots, and Bologna take 13-14 a game themselves. A Roma side four days before Sporting may rotate a little, which keeps this small.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. I lean slightly higher, as Roma's away games have averaged almost 11 on target, with Malen leading Roma's scoring. Bologna's home games have averaged about nine.
